items.question: What do I need to rent?
items.answer: A valid driver's license, passport or ID, and a security deposit may be required. Exact requirements vary by vehicle and will be confirmed before booking. To know the required documents and years of driving experience, contact us on WhatsApp or through the form.

items.question: How old do I have to be to rent?
items.answer: The driver must be at least 25 years old for cars and 16 for quads.

items.question: What is the security deposit?
items.answer: Deposit amounts are in US dollars (US$): US$1,000 for the Kia Seltos, US$500 for the other car models and US$300 for quads. For the scooter, the amount is confirmed before booking.

items.question: Is insurance included?
items.answer: Full insurance is not included in the rate. Coverage details and any deductible will be explained in your quote and rental agreement.

items.question: Can you deliver the vehicle?
items.answer: The vehicle is usually handed over at our office: Plaza Italia #22, Avenida Juan Pablo Duarte, Las Terrenas. Delivery to the airport is possible for a fee; contact us for the amount and the details.

items.question: How do I confirm my reservation?
items.answer: After your request, IVJ will confirm availability, total price, deposit and the steps required to secure the vehicle.

items.question: Is there a mileage limit?
items.answer: Contact us for the mileage conditions: we confirm them before booking.

items.question: Can I cancel my booking?
items.answer: Contact us for the cancellation conditions: we confirm them before booking.

items.question: What is the fuel and cancellation policy?
items.answer: Fuel, cancellation, late-return and damage policies will be provided with your final rental terms before you confirm. See also our Rental conditions page.

If you accept, Google Analytics measures page views and two actions: clicking a WhatsApp button and submitting a reservation request. These measurements contain no personal data (no name, phone or email). Advertising cookies stay disabled.
Your choice is remembered on your device. You can change it at any time with the “Manage cookies” link at the bottom of every page.
The internal administration panel is never tracked.

condiciones_items: Only the person who signs the contract is liable to the Company for payment of the agreed rate and for the expenses, damages and indemnities arising from the repair of the vehicle, including the days it is out of service for repair.

The client agrees to return the vehicle in the same condition in which it was delivered, at the place and time agreed in the contract; otherwise, the Company shall have the right to terminate the contract and recover the vehicle, regardless of who is in possession of it, at the client's expense.
The client shall not drive the vehicle until at least 24 hours after consuming alcoholic beverages.
The vehicle may not be used: 1) on a racing track; 2) to teach another person to drive; 3) as a taxi; 4) to push or tow another vehicle; 5) for any unlawful act punishable under Dominican law.
The vehicle shall be used on paved roads and highways; fuel and lubricant costs are the client's responsibility for the duration of the contract.

The client is not authorized to incur any repair expenses on the vehicle. In the event of theft, accident, or fire, the client must notify the Company and the National Police immediately, have a police report drawn up, and provide a copy upon returning the vehicle; the client remains responsible in all cases for paying the deductible set at the signing of this contract. If, as a result of an accident, the other party agrees to cover the damages, costs, and indemnities and the Company recovers the deductible, it will be refunded to the client in due time.

Under no circumstances shall the client abandon the vehicle anywhere, in order to prevent theft and/or loss of parts and accessories; violation of this clause voids the insurance coverage in the client's favor and makes the client liable for damages, costs, and losses.

A 16% tax required by the Government will be added to each invoice, along with any other tax, fee, or contribution currently in force or that may be established by the authorities and laws of the State.
The Company agrees to deliver the vehicle in condition to provide the agreed service and to arrange the legally required insurance.
The contract is signed by the client after inspecting the vehicle and finding it in satisfactory condition; the client becomes responsible for it from that moment on.

If the client changes the address stated in the contract, they must notify the Company immediately; failure to do so authorizes any member of the National Police to recover the vehicle, regardless of location, time, or who is in possession of it, and return it to the Company.
Any fine imposed or arising from the use or driving of the vehicle must be paid before the contract is closed.
If the vehicle is not returned to the Company by the agreed date, it will be reported as stolen to the National Police, with the signing client held responsible, along with all legal consequences.
Expenses incurred by the Company in searching for the vehicle shall be charged to the client.

All expenses, invoices, damages, and indemnities generated under this contract grant the Company a collection privilege over the client's movable and immovable property, under articles 583 to 625 of the Code of Civil Procedure, with all corresponding legal consequences, without prior authorization, this right constituting the executory title required for such actions.
The client agrees to pay 100 pesos for each license plate or sticker removed from the vehicle.
The Company is not responsible for items left inside the vehicle.
If the client decides to return the vehicle before the term agreed in the contract, the client will forfeit 80% of the remaining amount.

rentabilite.title: Profitability by vehicle
rentabilite.subtitle: Revenue, outstanding balances, and maintenance costs, per vehicle.
rentabilite.footnote: Revenue is the total price of non-cancelled reservations. The balance due is already included in that revenue — it's not extra money, just what hasn't been collected yet. The net result only subtracts logged maintenance costs; it doesn't account for other expenses (fuel, insurance, etc.). The purchase balance owed (entered on the vehicle's page) isn't affected by the period filter and isn't subtracted from the net result — it's a capital debt on the vehicle, not a period expense. Net after payoff is the only column that subtracts this purchase balance from the net result; with no balance entered, it simply matches the net result.

Upcoming and pending reservations are therefore included; their status is shown. The amount is the reservation price, not a collected payment: the database holds no recorded payments.

aide.page_subtitle: How to use the internal panel, with a mockup of every screen.
aide.c00_intro: The internal panel is separate from the public site. Each team member signs in with their own email and password, created by an administrator (see the Users section).
aide.c00_step1: From the public site, open the Admin link at the bottom of the footer — or go straight to /admin/login.
aide.c00_step2: Enter the email and password provided by an administrator.
aide.c00_step3: The account's role determines access: Admin sees everything, including Users and permanent deletions; Employee handles day-to-day operations without those two rights.
aide.c01_intro: The home screen after signing in: current activity and vehicle returns to keep an eye on, without opening every section.
aide.c01_step1: The three counters at the top summarize ongoing reservations, upcoming reservations, and vehicles available today.
aide.c01_step2: The Quick actions buttons open a new reservation or a new client directly.
aide.c01_step3: The Returns list flags vehicles due back, with an Overdue marker once the return date has passed.
aide.c02_intro: Every request submitted by a visitor through the public /reservar form lands here automatically, before becoming a confirmed reservation.
aide.c02_step1: A new request starts as New; mark it Contacted once you've replied to the client on WhatsApp.
aide.c02_step2: Click Convert to reservation to create the reservation: vehicle, dates, and client details are already prefilled.
aide.c02_step3: A request with no follow-up can be marked Rejected to move it out of the active list.
aide.c03_exemple_intro: Let's follow a concrete case. A client — Demo Client — books a Kia Seltos 2026 from August 27 to 31. The screens below are rebuilt to match this test exactly, step by step.
aide.c03_intro: A reservation goes through several stages before it's truly finished: creation, tracking its progress in the list, a contract signed by the client, then the vehicle's return recorded in the panel. Here's the complete process, from the first click to closing it out.
aide.c03_step1: Two ways to create a reservation: New reservation from this page (blank form), or Convert to reservation from a request on the public site — client, vehicle, and dates are already filled in.
aide.c03_step2: Fill in client, vehicle, dates, times, and pickup location; the price is calculated automatically from the rate grid and stays editable by hand.
aide.c03_step3: In the list, each reservation shows an automatically calculated phase: Upcoming, In progress, Overdue if the return date has passed without a recorded return, or Completed.
aide.c03_step4: Once the vehicle is back, open the reservation and click Mark as returned — that's what actually closes out the rental.
aide.c03_creer_note: 1. Create the reservation. The form groups client and vehicle, dates and times, then a price already calculated but still editable by hand (discount, special arrangement...).
aide.c03_suivi_note: 2. Track its progress. The list filters by number, client, or vehicle; each reservation's phase updates itself based on the dates, with no manual action needed.
aide.c03_finaliser_note: 3. Finalize. From a reservation's page: Finalize the contract prepares the vehicle handover (covered in the next chapter), View printable contract shows it exactly as it will be handed to the client, and Delete reservation stays reserved for administrators (cannot be undone).
aide.c03_rendu_note: 4. Mark as returned. The client brings the vehicle back: one click closes out the rental, and the button becomes Returned on [date] · Undo — reversible in case of a misclick.
aide.c03_video_caption: Silent, unedited video — the full flow recorded exactly as it happened in the real panel.
aide.c04_intro: A 14-day view of the whole fleet. A blue cell is a reservation, an orange cell is a manual block.
aide.c04_step1: A single click on an empty cell offers to create a reservation or a block for that one day.
aide.c04_step2: Click and drag across a vehicle's row to select several days at once.
aide.c04_step3: On release, the choice screen opens with the full range already filled in.
aide.c04_step4: Clicking an already-occupied cell opens the matching reservation or block directly.
aide.c05_intro: The full fleet, with each vehicle's operational status and today's availability.
aide.c05_step1: Three possible statuses: Available, Maintenance, Out of service — updated from the vehicle's page.
aide.c05_step2: A vehicle's page lets you add a photo and manage one-off blocked periods.
aide.c05_step3: A vehicle taken out of the fleet gets deactivated rather than deleted, to keep its history.
aide.c05_step4: Uncheck Active on its page and note the reason for removal (sold on 03/12, quad wrecked...) — handy for quads or old cars that get sold.
aide.c05_step5: Delete is still available but gets blocked as soon as the vehicle has a reservation, request, maintenance record, or blocked period on file; a message says so clearly and suggests deactivating instead.
aide.c05_retrait_note: Remove a vehicle from the fleet. On its page, uncheck Active and note the reason; Delete stays reserved for records with no history at all.
aide.c06_intro: The maintenance history for the whole fleet: oil changes, brakes, tires, repairs, inspections.
aide.c06_step1: New record to log a job: vehicle, type, date, cost, and the date the next maintenance is due.
aide.c06_step2: A job whose due date has passed is marked Overdue.
aide.c06_step3: A mistaken record can be deleted directly from the list.
aide.c07_intro: A client's page centralizes their details, documents (license, cédula, passport), and the full history of their past reservations.
aide.c07_step1: Search by name, phone, or email.
aide.c07_step2: Open a client's page to see their reservation history without looking it up in the reservations list.
aide.c07_callout: Deletion is protected. A client who already has reservations on file can't be deleted — the panel makes that clear, so their history is never lost.
aide.c08_intro: A saved guarantor means their details don't need retyping for every contract. Once created, they show up in a dropdown when finalizing a rental contract.
aide.c08_step1: Create a guarantor once: name, phone, ID number, address.
aide.c08_step2: In a contract, pick them from Saved guarantor — the fields fill in automatically and stay editable.
aide.c08_callout: Deleting a guarantor never touches a contract that's already signed. The details stay printed on the existing contract — only the link to their page is removed.
aide.c09_intro: The rate table by vehicle category, also shown on the public site. Three tiers based on rental length.
aide.c09_step1: An admin clicks a price directly to edit it.
aide.c09_step3: The Active column is also clickable for an administrator: one click activates or deactivates the category right away, no page reload needed.
aide.c10_intro: Managing the team's accounts. Only an admin sees this section.
aide.c10_step1: New user: name, email, temporary password to share through a secure channel, then role (Admin or Employee).
aide.c10_step2: Deactivate blocks sign-in immediately without deleting the account — reversible with Activate.
aide.c10_callout: An admin can't deactivate their own account, so they can't lock themselves out of the panel.
aide.c11_intro: From a reservation, Finalize contract opens the handover form: time, condition, amounts, guarantor, and accessories handed over to the client.
aide.c11_step1: Fill in the handover details, the deductible, the deposit (the balance is calculated automatically), and, if needed, pick a saved guarantor.
aide.c11_step2: Check off the accessories handed over with the vehicle.
aide.c11_step3: Save contract, then Sign on screen to have the client sign right on the device.
aide.c11_signature_note: Full-screen signing. On Sign on screen, the side menu disappears completely — useful when the tablet or computer is handed to the client to sign, without them seeing or touching the rest of the panel.
